breaker. He now has Lionel Messi in his sights
 Kane takes his tally of England goals to 92 against Croatia on Thursday Justin Setterfield/Getty Images 
 By Jack Pitt-Brooke Nov. 13, 2026 Updated Nov. 15, 2026 10:14 am EST Share article 37 The Athletic has live coverage of Spain vs England in Nations League clash.  
 There can never have been so much pageantry and ceremony dedicated to one player before an England game.
 When Harry Kane led out his team to face Croatia on a cold Wembley night on Thursday, he was immediately greeted by a huge tifo of himself in the west stand, marking his record 126th cap. He picked up his Ballon d’Or trophy , won last month, and proudly displayed it to the fans. He received a commemorative cap from previous record-holder Peter Shilton , a framed shirt from Prince William and a glass-encased football from Croatia great and one-time Tottenham Hotspur team-mate Luka Modric — a replica of the first football brought to his homeland by the English in 1880.
 Advertisement
 These were touching scenes, a fitting tribute to England’s greatest player of the modern era. There was genuine love and gratitude for Kane from the crowd. This is a historic moment for the Bayern Munich striker, whose family stayed for photos on the pitch long after the final whistle had sounded on England’s 2-1 Nations League victory . This was history, too, for the England team and even for English football. Fans in the stands for the pre-match ceremony will tell their children and grandchildren they witnessed it.
 Prince William, Prince of Wales, and Peter Shilton present Harry Kane with a special shirt before kick-off (Ben Stansall/AFP via Getty Images) And yet Kane also looked as if he was looking forward to referee Morten Krogh getting the game underway so he could get back to doing what he loves best: playing for England.
 Yes, Kane loves his records and statistics and achievements. He targets them and loves picking them off. But he never rests on any particular milestone for too long. He admitted on Wednesday that he “struggles to take it all in” and that it is his “natural mindset to look ahead”. He even said it may not be until he is on a break during the Bundesliga’s Christmas-time hiatus that being named the best men’s footballer on the planet in 2025-26 will truly register.
 So now that the Ballon d’Or has been won, and the England caps record has been broken, Kane will swiftly move on to other things. Winning the Nations League final next June is a motivating target for head coach Thomas Tuchel and this group. Victory against world champions Spain in Madrid on Sunday would be a big step in that direction, and would make England seeded for March’s two-leg quarter-finals.
 Did you expect Harry Kane to go on to greatness? Sebastian Stafford-Bloor Kane was England’s best player on Thursday in setting up that Spanish ‘final’, as Tuchel likes to call it. The only true moment of quality in the first half came when Kane, dropped back into midfield, played a clever diagonal through to Jude Bellingham, darting in down the right. Bellingham pulled the ball back to Morgan Rogers, who put England 1-0 up.
 Advertisement
 But another record is in play here, even with 126 caps in the bag: how far Kane can take the goalscoring tally. He broke through 53 goals —once the England goalscoring record — in March 2023, and since then he has sped up.
 Until recently, it felt fantastical that any English player could ever get close to a century of international goals. Wayne Rooney was a unique talent and managed 53. Sir Bobby Charlton and Gary Lineker gave everything for England and fell just short of their half-century. And yet Kane, through his availability, consistency, reliability, efficiency and relentless excellence, has redrawn what we thought was possible.
 Kane waves to England fans after leading his side to victory over Croatia (Justin Setterfield/Getty Images) When England won a penalty after Jarell Quansah was pulled back by Hrvoje Smolcic, Kane stood up to take and clipped it past Dominik Livakovic. That was his 92nd England goal. He now has 14 of them in 14 games this year. This makes it his second-best ever year, after the remarkable 16 in 16 of 2021. Kane is a big cricket fan who will be well aware of the concept of the ‘nervous 90s’, when a batter starts to look anxious as they close in on a century. But he does not look edgy in the slightest.
 We can even start to think about the next big question: when will Kane bring up his hundred?
 England will start 2027 with that Nations League quarter-final, play two matches of some form in June and then contest six qualifiers for the 2028 European Championship in the autumn. Even if the 33-year-old does not score in the Metropolitano stadium at the weekend, there is every chance he will get eight more goals over England’s 10 games next year. Even if he does not, he will surely knock them off before, or maybe during, those Euros, which England will co-host with the Republic of Ireland, Scotland and Wales. He could even do it here at Wembley, where England play so many of their matches.
 Advertisement
 That achievement may be greeted with as much ceremony as we saw last night. It would put Kane in a truly elite group. Only three players have reached three figures for men’s senior international goals: Ali Daei of Iran with 108, Lionel Messi with 126 for Argentina and Portugal’s Cristiano Ronaldo with 146. When Kane was at Tottenham, he would often talk about emulating the numbers Ronaldo and Messi were putting up, and the general reaction was to laugh. But now he is within reach of joining those two in a very special club.
 It is even imaginable that he might push towards Messi’s tally, although Ronaldo’s may be too far. Kane is 34 goals away now from 126. But he has scored his latest 34 England goals — taking him from 58 to 92 — in 43 games, over the past three years and five months. (His 58th England goal was scored in June 2023).
 Three years and six months from today would be during the 2030 World Cup finals. It feels certain, assuming Kane stays fit, that he will want to give himself a fourth World Cup; most likely a last shot at the tournament, as he’ll turn 37 a week after its final. And who knows? That could even be the year that he chases down the Messi total.
 But even if he does that, reaching a number nobody thought possible, further extending an England record that may never be broken, he will still be thinking about the next step.
